statement.text:
For a group G, a function ϕ : G → R is a quasimorphism if there is a least
non-negative number D(ϕ) (called the defect) such that |ϕ(gh) − ϕ(g) − ϕ(h)| ⩽ D(ϕ)
for all g, h ∈ G. A quasimorphism is homogeneous if in addition ϕ(g n ) = nϕ(g)
for all g ∈ G. Let ϕ be a homogeneous quasimorphism of a free group F . For any
quasimorphism ψ of F (not required to be homogeneous) with |ϕ − ψ| < const, we
must have D(ψ) ⩾ D(ϕ)/2. Is it true that there is some ψ with D(ψ) = D(ϕ)/2?
                                                                     M. Burger, D. Calegari
